input: The pinned source's 12,956-rune continuous LP2 text (source sections 7–15) and solved-LP1 unigram model. Both source stages share complete forward lag and reverse anti-diagonal scans but use different hypothesized pair laws.
stage_ac: For all forward lags 11 through N−11 and reverse anti-diagonals with separation at least 11, score diff, sum and sumrev key-reuse laws over shifts 0–28. Whole-diagonal F and best contiguous S; PASS ≥+30. Whole-diagonal exclusion ≤−10 only through control-supported Pmax. Original control grid: 11 named periods, 6 planted stretch lengths, two plaintext sources, two orientations, 10 periodic or 25 reuse draws per cell, four flat anti-doublet nulls.
stage_ad: The ciphertext serves as its own key at every forward lag and reverse anti-diagonal under diff, diffrev, sum and sumrev laws ×29 shifts. Same F/S thresholds and null gate. Original control grid: 13 named autokey lags, 5 planted reuse lengths, two plaintext sources, two orientations, 10 autokey or 25 reuse draws per cell, four flat anti-doublet nulls.
source_defect_and_repair: Pinned original full and quick modes both crash during planted reuse controls: `planted_S` passes a one-row table to AC `segment_stats`, whose cumsum output is hard-coded to 29 rows. In a temporary runtime only, replace that allocation with `table.shape[0]`. No source files are edited. Already checked: all 138 AC and 184 AD source control rows reproduce exactly after this repair. Full source scans and output writers remain unchanged; exact six published TSVs must agree byte-for-byte before a replay finding is accepted.
independent_checks: Validate canonical source runes against site export; independently recalculate declared pair combinations, score-law tables and selected forward/reverse F/S cells, including a planted fixture, rather than trusting only matching archived tables. Distinguish the two source screens; don't turn numeric setting counts into independent puzzle ideas.
limits: Both stages use a solved-LP1 unigram model, a flat anti-doublet null and fixed pairwise rules. A positive F/S screen would require subsequent held-out plaintext recovery; a nonpassing screen excludes only calibrated source laws and bounds. If any null crosses +30, the source declares the run void, not a negative finding.
